We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template (template_id 1914396) to the molecule given. The molecule is from make_7_lvl2-apply_template-1 answer: a list of two SMILES? Actually that answer is '[["Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1", "Nc3ccccc3N"]]' That's a list of list? It seems the input molecule is a pair? Wait the question: "Can you return all possible precursors of applying the template as the result of the task make_7_lvl2-template_search-1 to the molecule below?" The answer gave two SMILES: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc3ccccc3N". So the target molecule is likely a combination? Actually maybe the target is a product of a reaction between those two? But the template is Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid. However the template mapping includes a sulfonamide etc. The target molecule seems to be a sulfonyl aryl with a cinnamic acid moiety? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 . That's a phenyl with methyl, attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl bearing a trans-alkene carboxylic acid. So the template likely breaks the C=C and C-COOH bond etc to give precursors: an aromatic aldehyde (maybe the aryl with CHO) and malonic acid? But the template mapping suggests the forward reaction: aldehyde + malonic acid -> product. In retrosynthesis, we need to apply template to target to get precursors: the aldehyde and malonic acid. However the target also has sulfonamide linking two aryls. The template likely only applies to the cinnamic acid part: the fragment /C=C/C(=O)O attached to aromatic ring. So the precursors would be the corresponding aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde SMILES: c2ccc(C=O)cc2? But the aromatic ring is attached to sulfonyl group. The fragment is c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the aromatic ring at position where the alkene is attached. In product, the alkene attaches to aromatic ring at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is attached to the other phenyl (with methyl). So the sulfonyl group is linking the two phenyls. The aldehyde is on the second phenyl. So the aldehyde SMILES: "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" but also attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl attaches to the nitrogen of sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl is attached to the nitrogen, not directly to the aromatic ring. The aldehyde precursor would be the aryl sulfonamide? Actually the template likely only cares about the aromatic aldehyde moiety, not the sulfonamide. The aldehyde precursor would be "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" but also attached to the sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is attached to the nitrogen which is attached to the first phenyl. The aldehyde is on the second phenyl, which is attached to sulfonyl via the nitrogen? Wait the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen which is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl). The sulfonyl attaches to the second phenyl (c2...). So the second phenyl is attached to the sulfonyl via S(=O)(=O) to the nitrogen? Actually S(=O)(=O) attached to N and to aromatic carbon: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl is attached to N on one side, and to aromatic carbon on the other side (the second phenyl). So the aldehyde precursor would be that second phenyl with aldehyde attached to it, and also attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is part of the product, not broken. The template likely does not break sulfonyl. So the precursor aldehyde would be "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is attached to the aromatic carbon, not to the aldehyde carbon. So the aldehyde precursor SMILES: "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" but also attached to S(=O)(=O)N? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the aromatic carbon at position where the alkene is attached in product. In product, the alkene attaches to aromatic carbon (para to sulfonyl?). The SMILES shows c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl via the aromatic carbon? The S is attached to the aromatic carbon directly: S(=O)(=O)c2... So the aromatic carbon is bound to S. The alkene is attached to that same carbon? Wait aromatic carbon can have two substituents: one is S, one is the alkene. In SMILES, "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2" is a phenyl with substituent /C=C/C(=O)O at one position. The S attaches to the aromatic carbon preceding that? Actually the SMILES "S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(...)" means S attached to aromatic carbon at position 1 of that phenyl. So the phenyl has S attached, and also the alkene substituent at another position (para?). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with aldehyde at that position, still attached to S. So SMILES: "S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2". But need to include the N? The N is attached to S, not part of aldehyde. So the aldehyde precursor is "NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2"? Actually the N is attached to S, but the aldehyde precursor is just the aromatic sulfonyl fragment? In Doebner modification, the aldehyde is just the aromatic aldehyde, not sulfonyl. The sulfonyl is a substituent on the aromatic ring, but the aldehyde is on the same ring. So the aldehyde precursor SMILES: "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" with S attached? The S is attached to the ring, but the aldehyde is also attached. So the full fragment is "S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2". However the N is attached to S, but that N is part of the other phenyl. In retrosynthesis, we might keep the sulfonamide intact, so the precursor aldehyde includes the sulfonyl attached to N? Actually the product includes the whole molecule; applying template will cut the alkene and carboxyl to give aldehyde and malonic acid, but the rest of molecule remains unchanged. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same molecule but with aldehyde instead of the alkene and carboxylic acid. So we need to generate that SMILES.

Thus we need to apply template to target using apply_template tool. Let's do that.
